answer: Rotating witness duty by verifiable randomness. Each epoch, a seed from a public beacon assigns every registered agent a random mesa of peers to audit, and the witness set for any vertex rotates unpredictably, so an attacker cannot pre-position identities where they will be checked. An identity failing its assigned audit loses its standing until it re-earns it through costly re-admission, and the basalt-like fixed cost of maintaining enough credible identities to survive random selection exceeds whatever the attacker gains.
